pr_title: lora: sx126x: don't re-enable interrupt in sleep
pr_body:
Don't re-enable the DIO1 interrupt when the modem is in sleep mode. This
fixes the power regression introduced in Zephyr v2.7.0.

Fixes #41026

Signed-off-by: Jordan Yates <jordan.yates@data61.csiro.au>

issue_context.title: LoRa: sx126x: DIO1 interrupt left enabled in sleep mode
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

When the sx126x modem is supposed to be in sleep mode, the DIO1 interrupt line is left enabled.
This results in additional power consumption on architectures where turning on interrupts is not free from a power perspective.

This regression was introduced in 74efaa920aed601440a40855f5934a82a9c27449.
Instead of turning on the interrupt before the work handler runs, which can then turn it off with a transition to sleep mode, the interrupt is always turned on after the work handler runs.

**Expected behavior**

Interrupt should not be left enabled.


**Impact**

Increased power consumption


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Zephyr v2.7.0

**Additional Context**

Simply moving the enable call back to where it was before does not seem to be a correct solution, as it looks like that would break the `sx126x_stm32wl` driver variant.

review_comments: Is the radio going to sleep state in the middle of the handler? Did you hit a scenario?

The issue mentioned in the comment says "...DIO1 interrupt line is left enabled. This results in additional power consumption on architectures where turning on interrupts is not free from a power perspective."

Guess it makes sense, what's the specific architecture scenario/setup? Don't think I've hit such a thing...

> The issue mentioned in the comment says "...DIO1 interrupt line is left enabled. This results in additional power consumption on architectures where turning on interrupts is not free from a power perspective."

I agree that turning ON the IRQ always in the IRQ handler for standalone radios is a waste of resources but I'm confused about the radio being in SLEEP state.

> Is the radio going to sleep state in the middle of the handler?

`Radio.IrqProcess();` is the place where the radio transitions to sleep mode, through
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/770732fe92faab44d93bcbc00fc4d45476c24dea/drivers/lora/sx12xx_common.c#L101
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/770732fe92faab44d93bcbc00fc4d45476c24dea/drivers/lora/sx126x.c#L286-L290

Unconditionally turning on the interrupt after those handlers run is just overriding the `MODE_SLEEP` logic. This can be easily seen by putting a `printk` inside `sx126x_dio1_irq_enable` and `sx126x_dio1_irq_disable` and running the `samples/net/lora/send` sample.

> Did you hit a scenario?

This is not some edge case, it is every single time you call `lora_send` or `lora_receive`

> Guess it makes sense, what's the specific architecture scenario/setup? Don't think I've hit such a thing...

nRF52 microcontrollers pay a penalty of ~20uA while any pin is configured as an edge-triggered interrupt (Requires the `GPIOTE` peripheral to be enabled)

Got it, so this makes a difference because it's the only GPIO interrupt in the whole application, hence shutting it off allows cutting power to the whole `GPIOTE` device. That's a good point, could not wrap my head around power consumption of individual lines, but this makes sense now, thanks for explaining.
